before.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=6x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=6y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?
before.html:
Question 1
?

{x′(t)=6x(t)y′(t)=6y(t) Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?

a
b
c
d
e
Submit

decision.explanation: The solutions are x(t)=x(0)e^{6t} and y(t)=y(0)e^{6t}, so every nonzero trajectory is a straight ray directed away from the origin. Option c shows these outward straight trajectories; e has curved trajectories and the other options point inward.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=6x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=6y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?
after.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=6$ with the corresponding eigenvectors $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

The general solution of the system is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{6t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{6t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]={e}^{6t}[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Notice that for each vector $[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ we get the straight-line solutions of the form
${e}^{6t}[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}]$
that represent the line passing through the origin and parallel to the vector $[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].$

Since ${e}^{6t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions move away from the origin as $t\to \infty .$

Among the given options, the only phase portrait satisfying these conditions is the following:
